Kind Message

This calculation used the first-cycle screening-dependent weights; the recorded screening residual remains relevant.

System

The system the job treated, its symmetry and its electrons; the method and basis are those of the input above.

  • N_\alpha and N_\beta count spin-up and spin-down electrons; together they are the nuclear charges Z_A less the charge q.
  • Their difference fixes the spin projection M_S=(N_\alpha-N_\beta)/2; the usual highest-weight input has S=M_S.
  • Closed shells have doubly occupied orbitals; equal spin counts alone do not establish one.

N_\alpha+N_\beta=\sum_A Z_A-q,\qquad 2S+1=N_\alpha-N_\beta+1

Input

Link 0 commands

Link 0 is the part of each job before its route: it sets this job’s memory, processors and files. Every linked job has its own.

Route keywords and options

The route selects the method, basis and job type.

Internal options

IOp settings override defaults; meanings follow the IOps Reference.

Molecule specification

The job’s title, charge and spin multiplicity, and where Gaussian took its geometry from.

Starting geometry

The structure the calculation starts from.

Output

SCF convergence

The job recorded 1 self-consistent field solution.

Geometry optimization

Gaussian printed 1 convergence checks, in output order, against their limits:

  • Each energy E_n is measured from that of the last check printed, E_n-E_N, which is not assumed converged.
  • The forces are given by their largest value and their root mean square over the N coordinates the optimization uses: F_{\max}=\max_i\lvert F_i\rvert,\qquad F_{\mathrm{RMS}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}F_i^2}
  • Displacements \Delta q are in bohr for distances and radians for angles.

Vibrational frequencies

The latest analysis has 111 modes, 0 of them imaginary, shown with their IR intensities over approximate mid-infrared regions, unscaled:

  • Each wavenumber follows from the mode’s force constant k_k and reduced mass \mu_k: \tilde{\nu}_k=\frac{1}{2\pi c}\sqrt{\frac{k_k}{\mu_k}}
  • The IR intensity grows with the squared change of the dipole along the mode: I_k\propto\left\lvert\frac{\partial\boldsymbol{\mu}}{\partial Q_k}\right\rvert^2
  • A mode is imaginary when k_k<0, a direction of negative curvature.

Normal-mode frequencies

Negative wavenumbers mark imaginary modes, not absorption frequencies.

Normal-mode animations

The imaginary modes, the six lowest real modes and the four most IR-intense ones, each scaled so that its largest atomic displacement is

\max_A\lVert\mathbf{u}_{kA}\rVert=0.6\,\text{\AA},

with \mathbf{u}_{kA} the displacement of atom A in mode k.

Frontier orbitals

The highest occupied and lowest unoccupied levels, and their gap, which is not an optical excitation energy:

\Delta\epsilon=\epsilon_{\mathrm{LUMO}}-\epsilon_{\mathrm{HOMO}}

Levels near the gap, one column per symmetry:

  • Hover a level to name it; click it to highlight it.
  • Labels use C_{1} symmetry, with lowercase for orbitals and capitals for states.
  • Surfaces enclose the phases \psi>+\psi_0 and \psi<-\psi_0, holding 85\,\% of \int\psi^2\,\mathrm{d}V; the overall sign is arbitrary.
  • Parts by angular momentum l or atom A, with Mulliken shares summing to 100\,\%: \psi^{(l)}=\sum_{\mu:\,l_\mu=l}c_\mu\phi_\mu,\qquad w_{A,l}=100\sum_{\mu\in A,\,l_\mu=l}c_\mu(\mathbf{S}\mathbf{c})_\mu

Atomic charges and electric moments

Mulliken charges for the final evaluated geometry, when a matching SCF population analysis was printed:

  • Red atoms carry q_A<0, blue ones q_A>0 and white ones q_A\approx0, on a scale symmetric about zero.
  • Mulliken populations split shared density equally, \mathbf P being the density and \mathbf S the overlap matrix, so compare charges only within one method and basis.

q_A=Z_A-\sum_{\mu\in A}(\mathbf{P}\mathbf{S})_{\mu\mu}

The dipole moment of the same density, in its printed orientation:

\boldsymbol{\mu}=\begin{pmatrix}5.6212 \\ 8.9838 \\ -0.7773\end{pmatrix}\,\mathrm{D}=\begin{pmatrix}2.21155 \\ 3.5345 \\ -0.305813\end{pmatrix}\,e a_0,\qquad |\boldsymbol{\mu}|=10.626\,\mathrm{D}=4.18059\,e a_0

Static polarizability

The last complete response gives the static polarizability tensor and its isotropic average, with the defining energy derivative:

\boldsymbol{\alpha}=-\frac{\partial^2E}{\partial F_i\,\partial F_j}=\begin{pmatrix}1199.29 & 68.59 & -61.0122 \\ 68.59 & 305.131 & 14.9518 \\ -61.0122 & 14.9518 & 110.297\end{pmatrix}\,a_0^3,\qquad \bar{\alpha}=\tfrac{1}{3}\operatorname{tr}\boldsymbol{\alpha}=538.24\,a_0^3

Excited states and spectrum

The job solved for 10 excited states. The spectrum places each state at its wavelength \lambda_n with its oscillator strength f_n, over conventional ultraviolet bands.

Oscillator strength measures the transition dipole moment \boldsymbol\mu_{0n} between the ground state and state n, the matrix element of the dipole operator \hat{\boldsymbol\mu}=-\sum_i\hat{\mathbf r}_i (atomic units):

f_n=\frac{2}{3}\,\Delta E_n\,\lvert\boldsymbol\mu_{0n}\rvert^2,\qquad \boldsymbol\mu_{0n}=\langle\Psi_0|\hat{\boldsymbol\mu}|\Psi_n\rangle=-\int\mathbf r\,\rho_{0n}(\mathbf r)\,\mathrm{d}\mathbf r

In C_{1} every orbital is a and every state A, so symmetry forbids no transition; only f_n tells bright states from dark ones.

Each bar stacks the weights of one state’s transitions between orbital sets:

  • A transition’s weight sums over its printed configurations; an unrestricted job counts c_{ia}^2 per spin instead of 2c_{ia}^2: w=\sum 2c_{ia}^2
  • Configurations with \lvert c_{ia}\rvert<0.1 are not printed, so \sum w\le 100\,\%.
  • Dark states, f<0.001, are faded.
  • Labels use C_{1} symmetry, with lowercase for orbitals and capitals for states.

Orbitals of the transitions

Orbitals contributing at least 10\,\mathrm{\%} to a state:

  • Orange surfaces enclose \psi>+\psi_0 and teal ones \psi<-\psi_0, at the isovalue \psi_0 whose surfaces hold 85\,\% of each orbital’s density \int\psi^2\,\mathrm{d}V; the settings show and move it.
  • The colours mark the orbital’s two phases, not charge: an orbital’s overall sign is arbitrary, so they are kept apart from the red and blue of potentials and density changes.

Density change of each state

Density changes by state, with degenerate states grouped:

  • Blue surfaces enclose \Delta\rho<-\Delta\rho_0, where electrons leave, and red ones \Delta\rho>+\Delta\rho_0, where they arrive, at the isovalue \Delta\rho_0 whose surfaces hold 80\,\% of each state’s \int\lvert\Delta\rho\rvert\,\mathrm{d}V; the settings show and move it.
  • The densities come from the printed configurations, which leave out amplitudes \lvert c_{ia}\rvert<0.1.

Hole and particle densities integrate to one electron and average degenerate states.

\rho_{\mathrm{h}}=\frac{\sum_{ij}(\mathbf{X}\mathbf{X}^{\mathsf{T}})_{ij}\,\phi_i\phi_j}{\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{X}\mathbf{X}^{\mathsf{T}}},\qquad \rho_{\mathrm{p}}=\frac{\sum_{ab}(\mathbf{X}^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{X})_{ab}\,\phi_a\phi_b}{\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{X}^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{X}},\qquad \Delta\rho=\rho_{\mathrm{p}}-\rho_{\mathrm{h}}

q_{\mathrm{CT}}=\int\rho_{+}\,\mathrm{d}\mathbf{r},\qquad d_{\mathrm{CT}}=\lvert\mathbf{R}_{+}-\mathbf{R}_{-}\rvert,\qquad S_{\mathrm{hp}}=\int\sqrt{\rho_{\mathrm{h}}\rho_{\mathrm{p}}}\,\mathrm{d}\mathbf{r}

q_{\mathrm{CT}}, d_{\mathrm{CT}} and S_{\mathrm{hp}} measure transferred charge, centroid separation and overlap.

  • Each element R of C_{1} is coloured by \chi_\Gamma(R) of the level’s representation \Gamma.
  • A or B means \chi(C_n)=\pm1, g or u means \chi(i)=\pm\chi(E), and ' or '' means \chi(\sigma_h)=\pm\chi(E).
  • Rotation axes are long dashes, mirror planes short dashes, and i an open circle.
  • Each operation carries the molecule onto itself; a reflection plays as a flip about an axis in its plane, then the reflection left, and a rotation-reflection then rotates.

Checkpoints

Saved checkpoints, with energies and frontier gaps, in read/write order.

Technical details

The program, the resources and the timing of the calculation.
